text:
Even `/dev/urandom` and huge files exit 0 — as predicted, `fread` is hard-capped at 64 bytes. Let me do a systematic sweep of edge cases (boundaries, special files, FIFOs, procfs) to be rigorous before concluding anything.<action>
{"tool": "bash", "input": {"command": "cd /tmp 2>/dev/null; cd - >/dev/null; mkdir -p test && cd test
# boundary sizes 0..70
for i in $(seq 0 70); do python3 -c "open('sz$i','wb').write(b'B'*$i)"; done
# all byte values, NUL-heavy, high-bit junk
python3 -c "open('allbytes','wb').write(bytes(range(256)))"
python3 -c "open('nuls','wb').write(b'\x00'*64)"
python3 -c "open('ffs','wb').write(b'\xff'*64)"
# fifo
rm -f fifo && mkfifo fifo && (echo hello > fifo &) 2>/dev/null
# procfs / sys specials
candidates="sz0 sz1 sz63 sz64 sz65 sz70 allbytes nuls ffs fifo /etc/hostname /proc/self/status /proc/self/cmdline /proc/version /dev/full /dev/null /dev/stdin"
for p in $candidates; do
  ./vuln "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1; V=$?
  ./fixed "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1; F=$?
  if [ "$V" != "$F" ] || [ "$V" -ne 0 ]; then echo "DIFF/CRASH: $p vuln=$V fixed=$F"; fi
done; echo "sweep done (only diffs/crashes shown above)"
# also verify vuln's n value directly with a debug harness
cat > probe.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
int main(int c,char**v){FILE*f=fopen(v[1],"rb");if(!f){puts("openfail");return 2;}char b[64];size_t n=fread(b,1,sizeof(b),f);printf("n=%zu\n",n);return 0;}
EOF
cc -O0 -o probe probe.c && for p in sz64 sz65 allbytes /dev/urandom; do echo -n "$p -> "; timeout 2 ./probe "$p"; done"}}</action>
